answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a basalt as the anchor of the cost.
